guide: Open Start and check the yellow settings: the return target, the raise level, the conversion floor, the monthly ad budget and the highest ad share of royalties. They are your own numbers.
Check Titles, Editions, Stores and Platforms. They hold the prices, costs and royalty shares that every break-even figure reads (check each store's current terms).
Write each ad campaign in Campaigns with its title, platform, budget and bid. Add a row to Campaign Ledger, Maximum Bid by Campaign and Campaign Rank for a new campaign.
Enter the ad numbers every week in Ad Days: spend, clicks, sales, page reads and royalties. Everything else fills in by itself.
Read Campaign Rank from the top: the verdict says stop, hold or raise, and the budget a stop would free.
Use Break-Even by Edition and Maximum Bid by Campaign to set a bid under the highest cost per click that still meets your return.
Read Ad Compare with Own History and Conversion by Title each month: a fall beyond your limit or a conversion under your floor says where to look first.
Write each price promotion in Promotions with the copies before, during and after (equal periods). Promotion Results shows the extra royalties, the payback days and a repeat, change or skip verdict.
Test a price in Price Tests with equal periods. Price Test Comparison keeps A, keeps B or says test longer.
Fill Sales by Title and Month with your monthly totals so the ad share of royalties can be worked out. Figures from stores are estimates until the payment arrives.
Use the 18 tools to find a break-even bid, rank campaigns, split a budget, plan a launch ramp, test a promotion or a price and forecast the next 3 months.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a ready text to the ad specialist, the assistant or a partner.

Read the Ads Dashboard and the Charts every week. A first-time author with one campaign and one promotion a quarter uses the same sheets with a few rows; a small press reads the pen-name columns as author columns.

listing.title: Author Ads and Price Promotion Tracker Excel Template: Return on Ad Spend, Break-Even Bid, Campaign Ledger, Promotion Results
listing.headline: Know which book ad to stop, hold or raise, and which promotion to repeat
listing.description:
Run the advertising and price promotion side of an author or self-publisher business in one Excel workbook. Built for an independent author, a virtual assistant and the ad specialist who run campaigns on store ads, social ads and search ads and plan price promotions. Campaigns and Ad Days hold every campaign, its budget, its bid and the daily spend, clicks, sales, page reads and royalties. Campaign Ledger turns them into conversion, cost per sale, profit and the return on ad spend (royalties for every unit of spend), and Campaign Rank lists the worst running campaign first with a stop, hold or raise verdict and the budget a stop would free.

Break-Even by Edition and Maximum Bid by Campaign work out the royalty after cost and the highest bid per click that still meets your target. Ad Compare with Own History sets this month against the 3 months before and the same month last year, and Conversion by Title checks every title against your conversion floor. Promotions and Promotion Results show copies before, during and after, the extra royalties at the lower price, the page-read income moved, the payback days and a repeat, change or skip verdict. Price Tests and Price Test Comparison keep price A or price B.

18 tools cover the break-even ad cost, the stop, hold or raise ranker, campaign profit and loss, conversion, daily budget, cost per click ceiling, promotion result and fit, price change break-even, platform comparison, budget allocation, launch ad ramp, a 3-month forecast, ad share of income, page-read-aware return and campaign age. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the ad specialist, the assistant, newsletter partners, the web developer and the accountant.

This is part four of the Author and Self-Publisher Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Every target is your own number. It helps you keep track of your ads and does not promise income or sales; figures from stores are estimates until the payment arrives, and each store's current terms apply.

competitors.lacks: record income but never match ad spend to the royalties it brought, so no return, no break-even bid and no stop verdict
show spend and clicks of one store only, never the page reads, other platforms, your own history or what a stop frees
know categories and totals but not campaigns, conversion floors, price promotions or the royalty after print cost
list dates for a launch but never ramp the launch ad budget, check the platform minimum or compare promotions
charge a monthly fee that rises with your income and cannot test a price change or a promotion against your own earlier results

Royalty a day at price A: {col:pricecmp.royalty_day_a}. At price B: {col:pricecmp.royalty_day_b}. Change of B against A: {col:pricecmp.change}.

Price B needs {col:pricecmp.lift_needed} more copies to match A; it sold {col:pricecmp.lift_seen} more. The fewest copies in a period were {col:pricecmp.min_units}; a test needs at least {set:test_min_units}.
Verdict: {col:pricecmp.verdict}. Decision of the author: ____________.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business. Confirm anything about tax, contracts or store terms with your adviser and check each store's current terms.

documents.title: Ad budget plan for a month
paragraphs: Ad budget plan of {set:company} for the month starting {col:adsmonth.month}, dated {today}.
Monthly budget {col:adsmonth.budget}. Spend so far {col:adsmonth.spend}; spend this year up to this month {col:adsmonth.spend_year}.
Your limit for ad spend is {set:ad_share_limit} of all royalties (your own number). All royalties of the month so far: {col:adsmonth.all_royalties}.
Rule for the month: raise the campaigns that return {set:ad_raise_return} or more, stop the ones below {set:ad_return_target}, and keep the rest.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business. Confirm anything about tax, contracts or store terms with your adviser and check each store's current terms.

documents.title: Platform comparison report
paragraphs: Platform comparison report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Platform: {col:adsplat.platform}. Month starting {col:adsplat.month}.
Spend {col:adsplat.spend}, clicks {col:adsplat.clicks}, sales {col:adsplat.sales}, royalties with page reads {col:adsplat.royalties}.
Return {col:adsplat.return}, cost per click {col:adsplat.cpc}, cost per sale {col:adsplat.cps}. The return target is {set:ad_return_target}.
Compare this line with the other platforms of the same month in the Ads by Platform and Month sheet before you move any budget.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business. Confirm anything about tax, contracts or store terms with your adviser and check each store's current terms.

documents.title: Break-even sheet for the ads of one edition
paragraphs: Break-even sheet for ads of {set:company}, dated {today}. Edition {col:breakeven.edition_id}: {col:breakeven.title}, {col:breakeven.format}, sold through {col:breakeven.store}.

List price {col:breakeven.price}, unit cost {col:breakeven.unit_cost}, royalty share used {col:breakeven.share_used} (check each store's current terms). Royalty per copy after cost: {col:breakeven.royalty_per_copy}.

Break-even: ads may take {col:breakeven.break_even_share} of the price, which is {col:breakeven.break_even_cps} for each sale. Your target is {col:breakeven.target_share} of the price, which is {col:breakeven.target_cps} for each sale.
Verdict: {col:breakeven.verdict}. Page-read income, where the title is in a lending program, comes on top of the royalty.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business. Confirm anything about tax, contracts or store terms with your adviser and check each store's current terms.

documents.title: Brief for the ad specialist
paragraphs: Brief of {set:company} for {col:campaigns.specialist}, dated {today}. Campaign: {col:campaigns.campaign} for {col:campaigns.title} on {col:campaigns.platform}.
Daily budget {col:campaigns.daily_budget}. Bid per click {col:campaigns.bid}; please keep it at or under {col:campaigns.target_bid}, the target bid from the campaign's own numbers.

Goal: a return of at least {set:ad_return_target} royalties for each unit of ad spend. Conversion floor: {set:conversion_floor} of clicks. Tell me at once if conversion falls below it, because the product page may be the problem and not the ad.
Please send spend, clicks, sales and page reads every week, and tell me before you change a budget or a bid.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business. Confirm anything about tax, contracts or store terms with your adviser and check each store's current terms.

documents.title: Promotion schedule for newsletter partners
paragraphs: Promotion schedule of {set:company} for {col:promos.partner}, dated {today}.

Title: {col:promos.title}. Kind: {col:promos.kind}. The promotion runs from {col:promos.start_date} to {col:promos.end_date}. The promotion price is {col:promos.promo_price}, the normal price {col:promos.normal_price}.
We would be glad if you featured the book in your newsletter on the first day. Please tell us the day you choose and send us your link, and we will send the cover, the text and the store links.
Thank you for your support. We help you keep your readers informed and do not promise any result.
